On August 25 and 26, 2017, GEYK worked with the French youth climate organization CliMates to organize COP in My City in Seoul. COP in My City simulates the Conference of the Parties to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change and gave GEYK an opportunity to collaborate with CliMates.

We invited early GEYK member Kim Min-su, a specialist at Korea’s Greenhouse Gas Inventory and Research Center, to introduce international negotiations. On the first day we learned how negotiations work, explored the history of diplomacy, and considered what kind of negotiators we were. We practiced with scenarios ranging from selling a Cadillac to talks involving Korea, the United States, and Japan, and negotiations set during the Cold War and Korean War. On the second day we represented countries in a mock UN climate conference. Despite our efforts to reach agreement, the simulation projected a temperature rise of 2.2°C, which surprised everyone.

We shared what the exercise taught us and discussed what role young people should play. Under the new climate framework, countries have pledged voluntary emissions reductions and will need to do their utmost to protect the planet. We committed to doing our part as young people.

COP in My City in Seoul was a valuable experience, and we’re taking what we learned into our future youth climate work.
